content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Payment gateway

No-KYC payment gateways are not workarounds or creative alternatives, but a fundamental shift in digital commerce infrastructure. They enable creators to process payments without relying on platforms that demand Know-Your-Customer (KYC) information, thereby giving them full control over their sales data and eliminating the risk of being shut down at any moment. This infrastructure is not just about avoiding fees, but about reclaiming ownership and agency in one's digital business.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

At its core, this infrastructure leverages a combination of free and open-source tools, including GitHub Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage, and Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery. NOWPayments integrates with this stack via automatic on-chain crypto payment verification, allowing creators to receive payment in 300+ cryptocurrencies without incurring platform fees or sacrificing data ownership.
Who This Is Built For and Why

This no-KYC payment gateway infrastructure is specifically designed for digital creators who sell ebooks, courses, templates, fonts, presets, beats, plugins, and software in regions where Stripe and PayPal are unavailable or severely restricted. By providing a sovereign digital commerce stack, COREMERCH empowers these creators to build a sustainable business without relying on intermediaries, thereby breaking the cycle of exploitation and establishing a more equitable relationship between creators and their customers.
No-KYC payment gateways are not a workaround, but a fundamental shift in digital commerce infrastructure.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The order management layer gives you complete visibility into every transaction your store processes. In Stack 01, every order is logged to a Google Sheet with the buyer's email, product purchased, payment amount in crypto and USD equivalent, transaction hash for on-chain verification, and delivery status. In Stack 02, orders are stored in a Supabase PostgreSQL database with the same fields plus additional metadata. Both can be exported as CSV at any time. The transaction hash provides cryptographic proof of every payment that does not depend on any platform's records — you can verify any transaction independently on a public blockchain explorer.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

To deploy a sovereign digital commerce stack, follow these concrete steps: (1) sign up for a GitHub Pages account and configure your hosting; (2) set up Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic; (3) integrate NOWPayments for on-chain crypto payment verification; (4) connect Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage; and (5) configure Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery. Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy a sovereign digital commerce stack, follow these concrete steps: (1) sign up for a GitHub Pages account and configure your hosting; (2) set up Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic; (3) integrate NOWPayments for on-chain crypto payment verification; (4) connect Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage; and (5) configure Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery. With these steps, you can ensure seamless payment processing, secure data storage, and instant product delivery, all while maintaining your full ownership and control over your sales data.
Frequently Asked Questions
How do I integrate NOWPayments with my existing website?

To integrate NOWPayments with your existing website, you'll need to set up a webhook that fires the moment payment confirms on-chain, allowing you to receive payment in 300+ cryptocurrencies without incurring platform fees or sacrificing data ownership.
What are the recommended networks for low fees?
The recommended networks for low fees are BSC, Solana, and TRON, which incur transaction fees of under $0.10 per transaction, making them ideal for creators who prioritize cost-effectiveness.
Can I use this infrastructure to sell physical products?
While the infrastructure is specifically designed for digital products, you can modify it to accommodate physical products by using a fulfillment service that integrates with your backend logic.
How do I configure data encryption for my sales data?

To configure data encryption for your sales data, you'll need to set up a secure connection between your backend logic and your order storage solution, using a protocol like HTTPS or TLS to protect your data from unauthorized access.
What happens if I encounter technical issues?

If you encounter technical issues, you can contact our support team for assistance, who will work with you to resolve the issue promptly and efficiently, ensuring minimal downtime and maximum productivity.
